agents.name: compiled LangGraph BI agent

authority_facts.fact: The model is directly bound to execute_query, which passes the model-provided SQL string to SQLDatabase.run_no_throw against a PostgreSQL connection.
The same model is bound to QuickSight construction tools and build_compile, which writes analysis_json.json and calls client_qs.create_analysis.
Chainlit chat text and uploaded file content enter the LangGraph model/tool loop.

findings.claim: Model-selected SQL reaches a PostgreSQL execution primitive without a source-visible read-only restriction or approval boundary.
The agent can construct and create an AWS QuickSight analysis through model-selected tool calls without an explicit human approval gate.
evidence: app.py: QuickSight tools are bound to the model

findings.claim: Interactive chat/file content can influence model-directed database or QuickSight state changes; no application-level approval step is visible before those tools execute.
evidence: app.py: ToolNode executes model tool calls

controls: Database/QuickSight endpoints depend on deployment configuration; blank source defaults may make the sample non-operational until configured.
No process-execution primitive was found in the reviewed BICO tool surface.

controls: The current pinned source appears non-runnable due to an undefined settings variable; declared authority must not be reported as proven live runtime authority without acknowledging this.

authority_facts.fact: memory_orchestrator delegates to three specialist agents; ingest_agent writes persistent memory, consolidate_agent reads/writes consolidation state, and query_agent reads memory/history.
The legacy agent.py HTTP service defaults to public user mode when MEMORY_API_KEYS is empty, allowing unauthenticated ingest/query/consolidate requests.
The newer server.py surface requires authenticated JWT or API-key users for memory endpoints.
delete_memory and clear_all_memories are direct application endpoints/functions and are not bound as ADK agent tools in build_agents().

findings.claim: In the legacy agent.py service, absence of MEMORY_API_KEYS intentionally enables public mode; unauthenticated /ingest content reaches the orchestrator/ingest agent and store_memory persistent SQLite write.
evidence: agent.py: api_key_auth_middleware assigns DEFAULT_PUBLIC_USER_ID when no API keys are configured

findings.claim: Ingest and consolidation agents have persistent SQLite write authority with no separate human approval boundary.
The orchestrator can delegate into specialist agents spanning persistent memory read and write capabilities.

application_findings_not_agent_authority.claim: The legacy public-mode API also exposes /delete and /clear, but these call delete_memory/clear_all_memories directly and are not agent-reachable tools.

chain: unauthenticated HTTP /ingest when MEMORY_API_KEYS is empty

controls: Per-user paths and contextvars isolate data by resolved user_id.
server.py implements JWT/API-key authentication for the newer API surface.
Agent tool bindings do not include delete_memory or clear_all_memories.

authority_facts.fact: The default config fallback starts the local workspace MCP server and exposes every returned workspace tool to the model.
workspace run_python executes model-provided Python in a subprocess; cwd is confined to WORKSPACE_ROOT but the Python process itself is not sandboxed.
The /ws/agent WebSocket accepts connections and model prompts without an authentication check.
The workspace MCP also exposes model-selected HTTP(S) company-site scanning, workspace file read/write, and persistent research-note writes.
Alpaca/Robinhood trading tools have explicit source-level lock/filter controls and are not part of the default fallback workspace-only configuration.

findings.claim: Unauthenticated WebSocket prompts can drive a model that is bound to workspace__run_python, which executes arbitrary Python in a subprocess without a security sandbox or approval gate.
evidence: server.py: /ws/agent accepts then agent.run(prompt) with no auth check
agent.py: default fallback config binds workspace MCP

findings.claim: The model can choose the URL passed to scan_company_website; the scanner accepts arbitrary http/https hosts and follows redirects with no destination allowlist.
All tools returned by enabled non-trading MCP servers are passed to the model; dangerous workspace code/file-write tools have no per-action approval boundary.
evidence: agent.py: session.list_tools loop appends tools to self.openai_tools
agent.py: only Alpaca/Robinhood names receive _tool_allowed filtering

findings.claim: The unauthenticated WebSocket payload controls config_path, allowing a caller to choose which existing local MCP configuration JSON is loaded and thereby alter the agent's tool/server authority.

application_findings_not_agent_authority.claim: server.py exposes direct REST paper-order functionality without an authentication layer; this is application authority, not an agent tool path.

controls: workspace read/write paths are confined by safe_path, but run_python is not OS-sandboxed and can escape that filesystem intent.
Live trading tool exposure is guarded by environment confirmations and name-based filters.
Robinhood remote MCP is disabled by default unless explicitly enabled.
